title: 2018 Hurlstone Legal Studies Trial
notes: All 20 Section I questions and answers transcribed from the paper and its answer key (page 18). No stimulus groups or non-text figures occur in the multiple-choice section.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a complete defence to a crime?
Who has the burden of proof in a Local Court?
Which of the following would be a mitigating factor during sentencing?

options.B: History of mental illness of the victim
options.C: The use of a weapon during the offence
options.D: The relatively young age of the offender

questions.stem: Judy is 8 years old, Judy with two of her friends are caught stealing a truck. Why can’t Judy be charged with this offence?

options.A: Aggravating factors will prevent her being charged
options.B: The concept of doli incapax applies
options.C: Judicial discretion will prevent her being charged
options.D: Mitigating factors, such as peer pressure, will prevent her being charged

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of punishment?
When can the prosecution appeal to a higher court?

options.B: The defendant has committed further offences
options.C: The prosecution believes the sentence is manifestly inadequate
options.D: The defendant commits perjury while on the witness stand

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics illustrates that human rights are an automatic entitlement for all?
Which of the following legal concepts places the greatest restriction on judicial discretion in sentencing?
Which of the following is an alternative method of sentencing?
What is the role of the jury in a criminal trial?

options.A: Determine the sentence of an accused
options.B: Listen to the case and determine if an appeal can occur
options.C: Determine what evidence is presented during the trial
options.D: Listen to the case and determine verdict

questions.stem: Which of the following is an intergovernmental organisation that promotes and protects human rights?
Which of the following organisations is most capable of prosecuting individuals accused of serious breaches of human rights?
Which of the following is a statutory authority that assists individuals with human rights violations?

options.D: The International Committee of the Red Cross

questions.stem: What is the purpose of charge negotiation?

options.A: To involve the victim in determining the outcome
options.B: To provide training in negotiation for the police
options.C: To ensure that justice is achieved
options.D: To reduce costs and delays in the court system

questions.stem: Statement 1: In NSW, an accused person has the right to silence. Statement 2: Human trafficking is a transnational crime.

options.A: Statement 1 is true and statement 2 is false
options.B: Statement 1 is false and statement 2 is true

questions.stem: What is the process by which one country apprehends and sends a person to another country for the purpose of criminal prosecution?
What is the process used with juvenile offenders that involves a conference attended by the offender, the victim and other supporting members of society?
Which group of rights has the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights contributed to?

options.A: Maternity leave, right to work, right to form trade unions
options.B: Freedom, right to name and nationality
options.C: Right to speech, freedom from torture, fair hearing
options.D: Right to self-determination, right to life, freedom

questions.stem: NSW and Commonwealth law allows a suspected terrorist to be instructed to wear a tracking device if there is a genuine threat of a terrorist act. What is such an order called?
questions.answerNote: The printed key gives C (Preventative Detention), but wearing a tracking device is a control order, so the key looks wrong. A is a reasoned answer.

questions.stem: Which institution has the discretionary role to determine the early release of a prisoner before completing their full sentence?
